| [0003](./0003/) | cli | superseded | major | partial | 2026-07-26 — SUPERSEDED by 0010 (Module and Catalog Identity) and 0011 (Module and Catalog Publishing). The reason is scope rather than error: this entry began as a naming convention, absorbed version agreement, then absorbed the question of whether a version belongs in identity at all, then the question of how identity reaches an artifact — four problems on one id, with 27 decisions and six reversals among them. The append-only log did its job; what broke is that the narrative documents stopped tracking it, so 02-design still describes the version-agreement design under a revision banner and 05-risks carries tables a later decision invalidated. Rewriting in place was rejected because it would require breaking the append-only rule to produce a document that still spans four problems; deleting was rejected because the measurements are the expensive part and core carries a shipped, now-reverting change (nameSnakeCase, added 2026-06-17) whose only explanation lives here. The split follows the repo boundary and the sequencing boundary: 0010 owns what identity IS and how it reaches the artifact's bytes (a breaking core change that can be accepted without answering registry credentials), 0011 owns the commands that write it and the registry it goes to (a cli feature that depends on 0010). Both successors carry fresh decision logs starting at D1 with only current answers, and the evidence this entry gathered is restated inline there and dated rather than cross-referenced, so neither successor requires reading this one. This entry is now the record of how the design got here; experiments/ and research/ stay with it. | OPM Module Publishing Workflow |

| [0010](./0010/) | core | draft | major | not-started | 2026-07-27 — OQ walk: D16-D21 locked; OQ1/OQ3/OQ4/OQ6/OQ8 resolved; OQ9 and OQ10 filed. D16 gives #Catalog no `name` field — measured, nothing reads one in Go or CUE, and the catalogs already carry the kebab->snake projection D8 deleted (leaf `opm-experimental`, `package opm_experimental`) invisibly, because consumers import a catalog's `resources`/`traits` subpackages and never its root. D17 puts the primitive-under-catalog-path rule in 0011's PUBLISH GATE rather than in core, because core cannot express it where the primitives live: `requiredResources?: [#FQNType]: #Resource` holds a catalog's own resources and foreign ones as identical values, so a constraint reached through #transformers would enforce the rule by FORBIDDING 0001 D16's cross-catalog references. Recorded explicitly as NOT delivered: `which catalog ships FQN X` with no platform in hand, since resources sit at `.../opm/resources` while blueprints sit one segment deeper at `.../opm/blueprints/workload`, so no fixed kind-segment count exists. Stale `opmodel.dev/opm/...` doc examples fixed in core/src/{resource,trait,blueprint,transformer,types}.cue (spec-neutral). D18 resolves the live-instance migration as SUBSUMED: the entire deployed fleet (`opm-releases/` five environments, `northbyte/deployments/`) pins `opmodel.dev/core/v1alpha1@v1` — nothing is on core@v1, so there is no instance whose identity this entry changes. Two findings recorded as inputs to the future v0->v1 migration: relabel in place NEVER recreate, because opm-operator sets no ownerReferences and ModuleInstance has no finalizer, so deleting the CR garbage-collects nothing and the new instance can never prune the survivors; and the positive check stands, since a skipped prune emits no Event, status field or metric. D19 accepts a moved-ahead dev checkout and warns rather than versioning around it — 0011 experiment 02 measures that publish REFUSES a catalog with a local override even with --allow-local-override, and 0003 experiment 04 measures that the one-hop dev loop already renders local module bytes against the PUBLISHED catalog, so the residue is a developer's false conclusion, addressed by a file-presence check on cue.mod/local-module.cue at render. D20 AMENDS D1: a primitive's modulePath is a PACKAGE path with no @vN, split into #PackagePathType, because D1 widened one shared type and dragged the major onto fields that never read it — the pre-amendment #PrimitiveIdentity computed `_ref.major` and never used it, and a @vN module publishes vN.* tags so `version` already implies the major. This SHRINKS the migration: primitive modulePath values are unchanged from what ships today. D21 resolves OQ6 by keeping `version` required and moving `fqn` from a core derivation to a value each catalog AUTHORS from its identity package, so modulePath, version and fqn all read from one source and a release moves every key by one edit. The cost is measured and accepted: the derivation catches a disagreeing author at the catalog's own cue vet (`conflicting values`), whereas an authored FQN carrying a stale build passes `cue vet -c` with exit 0 — enforcement therefore MOVES to 0011's publish gate (#PrimitiveFQNGate), joining D17's rule in one mechanism. Both rejected alternatives were measured rather than argued: removing `version` leaves a stale key vetting clean, and deriving `version` from `fqn` is a CUE cycle. New: OQ9 (core/src/helpers_autosecrets.cue hardcodes `opmodel.dev/opm/resources/config/secrets@1.0.0` as a LIVE value, which no catalog ships and which D13 makes permanently unmatchable — core naming a catalog primitive is a layering inversion) and OQ10 (ModuleInstance has no finalizer and no ownerReferences, so deletion leaks every resource; ownerRefs cannot be the whole fix because modules render cluster-scoped resources a namespaced CR cannot legally own). | Module and Catalog Identity |
| [0011](./0011/) | cli | draft | minor | not-started | 2026-07-26 — Initial design recorded as D1-D7 with six open questions. The entry defines how an OPM artifact reaches a registry: one publish pipeline serving two artifact types (D1), which DERIVES its coordinates from the artifact and never rewrites the artifact to fit a coordinate (D2); version authoring split from version publishing, so a commit can sit between deciding a version and pushing one (D3); a refusal to publish an artifact whose identity is not concrete, closing the measured gap that `cue mod publish` will happily push a tree with unfilled identity fields (D4); a central registry that HOSTS rather than indexes, with owner-scoped module paths under reserved namespace segments (D5); and a local-override gate that never honours cue.mod/local-module.cue, with an explicit escape hatch for modules and none at all for catalogs, because a catalog's divergence propagates into the key space of everything built against it (D6). The four questions that block promotion are the ones this entry cannot answer from inside itself: publishing credentials, tag immutability, what replaces the modules repo's checksum-driven bump, and how the published fleet moves to the owner-scoped namespace. | Module and Catalog Publishing |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
